_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Based on pelican-eggs/chatbots (MIT).
name: VoiceTwine
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: VoiceTwine is a Discord bot that creates temporary voice channels for members as they join, and removes them when they empty. The egg runs it with SQLite or a MariaDB database.
startup: h="$(cat package.json pnpm-lock.yaml | sha256sum | cut -c1-64)-$(node -v)"; if [ "$h" != "$(cat node_modules/.raptor-installed 2>/dev/null)" ]; then echo "Installing dependencies"; COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0 corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --reporter=append-only --config.confirmModulesPurge=false || exit 1; echo "$h" > node_modules/.raptor-installed; fi; node node_modules/sequelize-cli/lib/sequelize db:migrate || exit 1; exec node dist/app.js

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# VoiceTwine: downloads the VoiceTwine release (already built) from its
# GitHub releases and checks it against GitHub's checksum. The database and
# .env are never touched; dependencies are installed by the server when it
# starts, for the Node.js it runs.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

repo=Twijn/VoiceTwine
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
# GitHub releases, through the installer's gh-release (GitHub's API has a
# low anonymous limit). gh_tag <latest|tag> prints the release's tag;
# returns 1 when there's no such release, 2 when GitHub can't be reached.
gh_tag() {
    local out
    out=$(gh-release tag "$repo" "$1" 2>&1) && { echo "$out"; return 0; }
    case "$out" in *"has no release"* | *"no releases"*) return 1 ;; *) return 2 ;; esac
}
offline="GitHub can't be reached right now, or is limiting downloads. Reinstall to try again in a few minutes."
version="${VERSION:-latest}"
case "$version" in latest|v*) ;; *) version="v$version" ;; esac
rc=0; tag=$(gh_tag "$version") || rc=$?
if [ "$rc" = 1 ]; then
    latest=$(gh_tag latest) || fail "$offline"
    fail "VoiceTwine has no version ${VERSION}. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as $latest."
fi
[ "$rc" = 0 ] || fail "$offline"
version=$tag
assets=$(gh-release assets "$repo" "$version") || fail "$offline"
sum=$(awk '$1 == "voicetwine.tar.gz" { print $2; f = 1 } END { exit !f }' <<<"$assets") ||
    fail "VoiceTwine $version has no release download. Choose a newer version."

if [ "$sum" != - ] && [ -f dist/app.js ] && [ "$(cat .raptor-voicetwine 2>/dev/null)" = "$sum" ]; then
    echo "VoiceTwine $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading VoiceTwine $version"
    tmp=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
    rm -rf "$tmp" && mkdir -p "$tmp"
    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
    gh-release download "$repo" "$version" voicetwine.tar.gz "$tmp/vt.tar.gz" || fail "The download failed or didn't match GitHub's checksum. Reinstall to try again."
    mkdir "$tmp/x"
    tar -xzf "$tmp/vt.tar.gz" -C "$tmp/x"
    [ -f "$tmp/x/dist/app.js" ] || fail "The download has no dist/app.js in it. Choose another version."
    # The built code is replaced as a whole, so no file of an older version stays behind.
    rm -rf dist
    cp -a "$tmp/x/." .
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    echo "$sum" > .raptor-voicetwine
fi
echo "Installed VoiceTwine $version. Set the Discord bot token and client ID, then start the server."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The VoiceTwine version to install, such as 1.4.1, or latest.

variables.name: Discord bot token
variables.description: The bot's token, from the Discord developer portal (Bot page).

variables.name: Discord client ID
variables.description: The application's ID, from the Discord developer portal (General Information page).

variables.name: Database type
variables.description: sqlite keeps the database in a file in the server's folder; mariadb uses the MariaDB or MySQL database set below.

variables.name: Database host
variables.description: The MariaDB server's address, when the database type is mariadb.

variables.name: Log level
variables.description: How much VoiceTwine logs: debug, info, warn or error.

variables.name: Node environment
variables.description: development logs readable lines; production logs JSON, for log collectors.
